sonnet.problem: The card ends with "Broken cisterns, part two," which says that going to Egypt and Assyria for water is the same as the broken cisterns of verse 13. Verse 18 never makes that link, so the card closes off a connection the text leaves open.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

sonnet.problem: The card tells verse 16, the shaved head, in the middle of the devastation of verses 15-16 (land laid waste, cities in ruins). It adds a joke about the word "shaved" to that moment.
sonnet.rule: A card that tells death, violence, abuse, serious sin or the body's private matters has no joke.

sonnet.problem: The question asks what the LORD asks next after "Is Israel a slave?" That makes the baker guess the next words of the line, and the story card gave no setup for the third question.
sonnet.rule: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
